structured.approach:
I followed the DE-04 procedure in the data-engineering-steps skill. First I read the four contracted inputs: feat.tasks, feat.design, org.data_model and task.repo_access. Then I read the existing ap_pipeline sources and pipelines: the tool view of ingest, transform, dq, pipeline, schedule.json, __init__ and the tests, plus ci.py and data/sample_feed.csv, which I opened with Read and Glob. The G9 hook blocks shell commands in this step.

I took background from journey:feat.clarifications (the CL-DE answers) and journey:task.db_changes, both read through context_get with receipts. For secrets in all environments I used the approved DE-02 task.secrets_scope file. I classified each existing element by layer and chose the smallest change set. There is no new source or pipeline, and parse_feed is unchanged because it is header-driven. The optional column is let in with an additive update to transform.to_model (TSK-01). The new delays.py (TSK-02) is listed and left to DE-07 for detail.

The output file already held a stale DE-07 version from an earlier run, and I overwrote it with the DE-04 content. A verifier subagent then checked the draft. It found three issues, which I fixed: the source for "empty when unpaid" is now record:memory, the line about CI and tests is now labelled as agent judgement, and I added the context_list citation for the input commits. No connectors were needed.

claims.text: The ingestion entry point parse_feed uses csv.DictReader over io.StringIO and returns one dict per row keyed by the header. It reads no column by name, so a v3 paid_date column passes through without a code change.

transform.to_model today builds id, vendor, due_date, amount and paid inside one try block. It rejects rows on KeyError, ValueError, InvalidOperation or AttributeError, using the exception type name as the reason.

The minimum ingestion-side change is an additive update to to_model. It adds PAID_DATE_REASON and _parse_paid_date, and parses paid_date only after the existing try succeeds, so an invalid value is rejected with reason 'paid_date' rather than 'ValueError'.
ingest.py, dq.py, pipeline.py and schedule.json are on TSK-01's 'Must not change' list, and the design marks parse_feed, quality_report and run as unchanged (HC-3).
TSK-02 creates the new module src/ap_pipeline/delays.py with delays_by_vendor, a pure function that returns Dict[str, List[int]] from paid records that have a paid_date.
The schedule stays daily at 02:00 Asia/Kolkata.
The checked-in sample feed has the v2 header invoice_id,vendor,due_date,amount,paid, with no paid_date column.
The registered Invoice model has paid_date as date or None, added in feed v3.
The ap_pipeline version is 0.4.0, and TSK-01 owns the version step.
No secret is required or granted for ap_pipeline in development, integration (dev) or production (main), so there is no gap.
No database change is needed, and the design adds no storage, service or library.
CI requires coverage of at least 90.0 and runs static checks for print, eval, exec, bare except and lines over 140 characters.
Feed v3 in production (PQ-6) gates release, not coding; the lane builds on synthetic v3 rows.
The requirement states that paid_date is an optional ISO date column that is empty when unpaid.

open_questions: CQ-I1: Is the v3 header spelled exactly 'paid_date'? parse_feed matches header text exactly, so a different spelling would load silently as paid_date = None. Interim answer: yes, as in org.data_model. Owner: Data engineering lead / feed owner.

CQ-I2 (carried DQ-1): Which production component fetches the feed and calls pipeline.run and delays_by_vendor? Interim answer: only the end-to-end harness wires the stages in this feature. Owner: Architect.
CQ-I3 (carried OQ-B6): Should an unpaid row that has a paid_date be rejected? Interim answer: it is accepted and the date is kept (DD-7). Owner: Product / Architect.
CQ-I4: Should data/sample_feed.csv gain a v3 example? It is outside the task file budgets. Interim answer: no change. Owner: Data engineering lead.
structured.summary:
I wrote task.components for DE-04. Result: the ingestion layer needs no code change and there is no new source or pipeline. The vendor CSV feed stays the only source, and the header-driven parse_feed already carries the optional v3 paid_date column. The minimum change set is:
- an additive update to transform.to_model (TSK-01), which parses paid_date after the existing try and rejects an invalid value with reason 'paid_date';
- one new pure module, delays.py (TSK-02), which DE-07 details.

dq.quality_report, pipeline.run, schedule.json (daily 02:00 Asia/Kolkata) and the v2 sample feed stay as they are. No secret is required or granted in development, integration or production. The file also lists the file budget, the must-not-change files, risks, the hand-off to DE-05, DE-07 and DE-08, and four non-blocking open questions; the main one is the exact spelling of the v3 header. A stale DE-07 version of the output file from an earlier run was overwritten. There are no blocking questions.
